column1: # Per-release annotation (GTF) sources, one row per (assembly, source, release,
# flavour). Consumed by scripts/download_annotations.sh and, for provenance, by
# scripts/make_sexaware_gtf.py.
# This is a SEPARATE file from config/sources.tsv on purpose: that one is keyed
# (assembly, source) and download_references.sh looks a row up with
# `awk '$1==a && $2==s {print $4}'`. Adding GTF rows there would make that
# predicate match several lines, so URL would become a multi-line string and the
# wget would fail confusingly.
# Release choice: the current release, plus the 1-2 older ones the ecosystem is
# actually pinned to (GENCODE / Cell Ranger vintages). Keep the FASTA rows in
# config/sources.tsv in step with these -- an assembly label is stable across
# releases, the sequence and the contig set are not.
# Flavour. We ship `primary`, the file that matches dna.primary_assembly:
#   primary  <Species>.<ASM>.<REL>.gtf.gz          chromosomes + scaffolds
#   chr      <Species>.<ASM>.<REL>.chr.gtf.gz      chromosomes only
# NEVER chr_patch_hapl_scaff (adds patches/haplotypes that are absent from
# primary_assembly) and NEVER abinitio (ab-initio predictions, not the genebuild).
# download_annotations.sh refuses those two patterns whatever this file says.
# Columns (tab-separated):
#   assembly            Assembly key (matches config/assemblies.tsv)
#   source              Annotation provider (ensembl)
#   release             Provider release number
#   flavour             primary | chr
#   is_latest           1 for the newest release shipped for this assembly
#   restrict_to_genome  1 if this GTF annotates contigs absent from the
#                       primary_assembly FASTA, so make_sexaware_gtf.py must
#                       drop them instead of failing. Verify before setting it.
#   url                 GTF download URL
#   checksums_url       Ensembl CHECKSUMS for that directory (BSD `sum` format)
#   notes               why this release is shipped
